data.title: Ansem Says Time Is a Key Risk-Management Factor in Short-Term Trading
data.description: Crypto trader Ansem shared his approach to managing risk in short-term trades. According to ChainCatcher, he said traders should consider time—not just price and stop-loss levels—when assessing whether a trade is working. When he enters a trade, he expects a clear market move to develop quickly; if Bitcoin stays near his entry price for an extended period without moving as anticipated, he reassesses the trade. He may exit early if the expected move fails to materialize, even if his stop-loss has not been triggered. Ansem said short-term trading can help traders identify sooner whether a strategy is working, and that deciding whether to hold a trade should take into account how long the market takes to meet expectations as well as its price action.

data.title: AI Agents Could Book the Wrong Flight, Raising Payment Liability Questions
data.description: Daniel Ishag, Bakkt’s chief commercial officer, described a hypothetical in which an AI agent books a flight to North Korea instead of South Korea, highlighting the risks of letting software spend autonomously. BeInCrypto’s State of AI Agent Payments 2026 found 14 of 19 reviewed products and workflows could act within preapproved permissions, according to BeInCrypto, while two incidents examined in the report sent $281,200 to attackers before recoveries. Stripe’s Link terms make users responsible for connected-agent transactions, including unintended ones, except in cases of Stripe’s own technical failure or error.

data.title: Gaurav Khanna, Shraddha Arya's new TV serial titled 'Dil Ki Bewafaiyaan', to be out post Diwali probably
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 31 -- Finally, the title of actors Gaurav Khanna and Shraddha Arya's upcoming TV serial has been revealed.

Soon, Gaurav and Shraddha will be seen in Star Plus' show 'Dil Ki Bewafaiyaan'. On Friday, the makers unveiled the show's promo.

Check it out here.

Produced by Ektaa Kapoor's Balaji Telefilms, the upcoming romantic family drama brings the actors together onscreen for the first time and marks their return to daily fiction following Anupamaa and Kundali Bhagya, respectively.

While Shraddha reunites with Balaji for her second collaboration after her long association with Kundali Bhagya, Gaurav begins his first project with Ektaa.

Gaurav and Shraddha recently participated in a puja ahead of the venture, with pictures and videos from the occasion circulating on social media. While filming is yet to begin, the Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2 set is being revamped for the production.

'Dil Ki Bewafaiyaan' is being planned for a post-Diwali launch, tentatively in the last week of November, and is expected to take the 9 PM slot on Star Plus. The channel is yet to announce the official premiere date and time.

Prior to Dil Ki Bewafaiyaan, Gaurav was busy with his reality TV commitments. Over the past two years, he participated in several popular shows, including MasterChef and Bigg Boss, emerging as the winner of both. He also participated in Khatron Ke Khiladi.

On the other hand, Shraddha was occupied with her personal life as she embraced motherhood. In November 2024, she welcomed twins, a baby boy and a baby girl.

data.title: "What's the hurry?": KTR questions IDBI Bank valuation, seeks answers from Centre over proposed sale
data.description:
Hyderabad, Oct. 31 -- BRS working president K T Rama Rao (KTR) has questioned the Union Government over the proposed sale of IDBI Bank, raising concerns about the bank's valuation, changes in the bidding process and the alleged failure to account for its valuable assets, including prime real estate in Hyderabad.

He has also sought answers on why the concerns raised by bank employees were not being addressed.

In a social media post, KTR said public sector undertakings (PSUs) and public sector banks were national assets that needed to be safeguarded.

Expressing concern over reports of alleged undervaluation of IDBI Bank, he questioned the rationale behind changing the rules and valuation methodology after the bids reportedly fell below the reserve price.

"Why were the rules and valuation methodology changed when bids fell below the reserve price?" he asked, seeking transparency in the disinvestment process.

KTR also drew attention to IDBI Bank's valuable real estate holdings, particularly prime land parcels in Hyderabad. He questioned whether the actual worth of these properties had been properly assessed and included in the overall valuation of the bank before proceeding with the proposed stake sale.

The BRS leader further questioned the Union Government's response to concerns expressed by IDBI Bank employees. He wanted to know why their objections and apprehensions were not being adequately addressed before taking a decision on the future of the public sector bank.

Emphasising that PSUs and public sector banks were national assets and needed to be protected, KTR said the Union Government owed the country clear answers before selling a reputed public sector bank to a private player.

He stressed the need for transparency and accountability in a transaction involving a major public sector banking institution and questioned the urgency behind the proposed sale.

Concluding his post with a pointed question to the Centre, KTR asked, "What's the hurry?"

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had placed IDBI Bank under its Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework in May 2017 due to its deteriorating financial condition. The restrictions were lifted in March 2021 following improvements in the lender's financial performance.

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (October 14) approved the sale of a controlling 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore, following which Life Insurance Corporation of India's (LIC) shareholding will fall to 19 per cent.

The restructuring follows a significant improvement in IDBI Bank's financial health, with gross non-performing assets (GNPAs) declining from 31.78 per cent in September 2018 to 2.32 per cent in March 2026. Net non-performing assets (NNPAs) also fell sharply from 17.30 per cent to 0.15 per cent during the same period, while the bank posted a net profit of Rs 9,513 crore in FY26.

data.title: Best of the week | A bell, family and a Rs.13 trillion promise: the week Jio went public
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Best of the Week is a weekly newsletter by Siddharth Sharma/Shravani Sinha. Subscribe to Mint's newsletters to get them directly in your inbox.

Some weeks, the market hands you a plot twist. This week, it handed you a family portrait.

On Wednesday morning, four generations of the Ambani family stood on stage at the National Stock Exchange as Jio Platforms Ltd stepped into public markets. Akash and Isha rang the bell at 10am. Mukesh Ambani, by all accounts, was moved to tears as his son Anant took the mic.

Anant put it the way only an Ambani could. For him, business is puja (worship), he said, and every puja ends with prasad. Today, Jio is shared with India. Isha spoke of a father who has found the courage, again and again, to build what others called impossible. Akash looked ahead: having democratized data in its first 10 years, Jio now wants to do the same for AI, cloud, connected devices and even connectivity from space.

Lovely speeches. But markets don't clap. They vote with money, and on Wednesday they voted loudly.

Jio opened at Rs.1,358, already 21% above its issue price. Then it kept climbing, closing at about Rs.1,417, up nearly 27%, on a day the Nifty slipped. By evening, Jio was worth around Rs.13 trillion, making it India's second-most valuable company, behind only parent Reliance Industries Ltd.

There was a juicy sub-plot, too. Listed Reliance companies together crossed Rs.30 trillion, while listed Tata companies stood at Rs.25.3 trillion. Reliance is now India's most valuable listed conglomerate, a crown the Tata Group had held until now.

Why does that matter beyond bragging rights? Because India's mega-IPOs have a habit of disappointing on day one. Mint's analysis found that none of the five biggest issues before Jio gained more than 2% on debut, and three ended below their offer price. Jio walked straight past that jinx. History also warns that a strong start isn't a finish. Reliance Power Ltd opened 21.7% above its offer price and still closed at a 17.2% discount. Coal India Ltd went the other way, widening its gains.

Two days after the bell, Jio reported its September quarter earnings on Friday, after market hours. It was its first report card as a listed company, and it delivered steady growth, backed by continued subscriber additions, growing traction in home broadband and sustained momentum in digital services.

Net profit came in at Rs.8,389 crore, up 13.7% from the same quarter last year and 8% from the previous quarter. Revenue from operations rose to Rs.40,475 crore, up 11.4% year-on-year and 3.3% sequentially. Jio credited subscriber additions, organic per-user growth and expansion in digital services.

For context, the June quarter had seen revenue of Rs.39,173 crore, up 2.4% sequentially and 12% on-year. Net profit was Rs.7,764 crore, up 9.2% on-year, though it had slipped 2.15% from the quarter before. The stock ended Friday 1.1% higher at Rs.1,437.50, ahead of the results.

Without a tariff hike, Jio's per-user growth from one quarter to the next has stayed largely flat for the past few quarters, and promotional 5G offers continue to hold it back. The Rs.300 Jio Prime membership, introduced in August, protects users from tariff hikes until 5 September 2027, and analysts expect it to have given some extra revenue support during the quarter.

Now back to the trading floor, because the debut had a few more surprises. Here's the oddly beautiful bit. Of every 100 Jio shares traded on day one, 71 were actually delivered, a sign that people were buying to keep, not to flip. One veteran market watcher put it neatly: those who got shares in the IPO don't want to sell, and those who missed out are chasing it. Two forces, one direction. That's what holds a price up.

A thin free float helped, too. With no promoter selling and only a sliver of the company available to trade, there wasn't much stock to go around.

Parent Reliance Industries, meanwhile, fell more than 3%. Analysts call it the classic holding-company discount. Once a subsidiary lists, the market stops stuffing its full value into the parent's price.

Now for the part that makes grown-ups nervous. Investors who missed the IPO borrowed to buy in. About Rs.2,227 crore of broker funding went into Jio on debut day, and 93% of the day's rise in NSE's margin book went to this one stock. Brokers happily offered the leverage once NSE put Jio in its highly liquid category.

Think of it as roughly 3-4% of a day's cash trading in the market, riding on one newcomer. Leverage is a lovely friend on the way up. On the way down, a 5-6% fall can bring real margin pressure.

Thursday offered a small preview of the nerves. Jio dipped about 2.5% to Rs.1,381 as some booked profits, then recovered to close at Rs.1,421.6.

Zoom out. At around Rs.13 trillion, Jio now sits in the same league as telecom giants such as Deutsche Telekom and AT&T, though China Mobile still leads. But Jio's yearly revenue is only about Rs.1.47 trillion, a fraction of what those giants bring in. So what are investors paying for? Not what Jio earns today, but what it could become. One strategist says the market sees Jio as a technology company, not just a telco.

Bharti Airtel Ltd earns better returns on its capital, 19% against Jio's 10.8%, and more per user each month, Rs.264 against Rs.215.6. Jio's trump card is sheer scale. With more than 533 million users, it is the world's second-largest operator in a single country after China Mobile.

Then there's the question of what Jio sells next. Telecom still brings in about 88% of revenue. Analysts want digital services, now just 12%, to become a real growth engine, and Jio says AI, cloud and connected devices are the next frontier.

How does Jio close the gap? Mostly by charging more. Airtel recently dropped its entry-level plan and raised postpaid tariffs. Jio hasn't followed yet. Analysts expect industry-wide hikes of 12-15% in the second half of this fiscal year, and Motilal Oswal is pencilling in a 15% hike for March 2027.

Worth remembering is that Jio's Rs.300 Prime membership, introduced in August, protects members from hikes until 5 September 2027. And new competition is circling, with Starlink exploring a broader mobile service.

So the party was real. The speeches were heartfelt, the numbers were record-breaking, and even a falling market couldn't spoil it. But Wednesday only proved that people want to own Jio. It didn't prove they'll still want to when the excitement fades, and the spreadsheets take over.

That's the story to watch, because the debut was never really the finish line. It was the starting gun. Jio now has to turn a Rs.13 trillion promise into earnings, returns and, eventually, price hikes customers are willing to pay.

Can it? Will tariffs rise in time? And how many of those leveraged bets survive a bad week?

This one has a long way to run.

India is among the world's biggest users of AI. Yet the computing power behind it mostly sits somewhere else. The country generates nearly 20% of the world's data but has just 3% of its data-centre capacity. More than $100 billion is now committed, with campuses rising from Visakhapatnam to Patna. Sounds like a win. But who captures the value, the ones who host AI, or the ones who build it? And these giant data centres are thirsty for power and water too. India may not need the world's biggest model to win. So what's its smarter play?

Bombay House is not backing down. Neither is Noel Tata. His latest nine-page letter, the fifth since the 17 September board meeting, calls the resolution reappointing N. Chandrasekaran "void" and wants every reference to it wiped from the minutes. He also questions the deciding vote and a business link that Mint first reported. Then comes the demand. Noel wants the meeting recording, the minutes and more, and he has given Tata Sons just seven days. Will the board hand them over?

Anup Bagchi got the keys to India's largest private bank on 27 October. The balance sheet is solid. Pretty much everything else needs attention. HDFC Bank's shares have slipped 6% this fiscal year, after falling 16% last fiscal year. The premium it once enjoyed over peers is shrinking. Controversies have piled up, and senior exits are making headlines. So where does a new chief begin? Rebuilding trust is one task. Keeping talent from walking out is another. And then there's the small matter of winning back the growth that made this bank the envy of its rivals.

Satish Patel grew up using the stream behind his Gujarat home. Today, he says, its water isn't fit even for cattle. He blames the solar giant across the water, Waaree Energies Ltd, a poster child of India's clean-energy push.

Mint's investigation, using documents obtained under RTI, found the factory was pulled up six times by the state pollution board in under two years. One notice ordered a shutdown. What exactly did regulators find? And did investors ever hear about it? Waaree didn't respond to Mint's questions. The villagers, meanwhile, are running out of patience.

Look at the Nifty and October seems fine. It's up nearly 2%. Now look under the hood. More stocks are falling than rising. On BSE, 2,709 declined against 2,399 that advanced, the weakest breadth in seven months. Oil near $115, a war that won't end, and stubborn global bond yields are doing the damage, while foreign investors have pulled out about $31 billion this year. The odd thing is, earnings are strong. Mint's analysis shows profits growing at their fastest pace in 10 quarters. So why isn't the market cheering?

India is considering whether AI platforms need a distinct legal definition and regulatory framework, as debates over a standalone AI law intensify. Big Tech firms favour sector-specific rules over broad legislation, arguing that sweeping regulation could stifle innovation. Lawyers, meanwhile, say existing intermediary laws need an overhaul to address AI-generated content and clarify liability. The central issue is whether AI platforms qualify for safe harbour protection, which shields intermediaries from liability for user content. With policymakers divided on the approach, the government is weighing how to balance innovation with safeguards against misuse.

India is stepping up oil palm cultivation to reduce its dependence on imported edible oils, which cost the country $18.3 billion in 2024-25. The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm, launched in 2021 with a Rs.11,040 crore budget, aims to boost domestic production by 2030-31.

Farmers are drawn by relatively stable, long-term returns, while companies such as Godrej Agrovet and Patanjali Foods are expanding plantations and processing infrastructure. However, reliable irrigation, suitable growing conditions, and higher yields will be crucial to sustaining the expansion and improving farmers' incomes.

China's inflation remains subdued despite rising global energy costs, with consumer prices increasing just 0.9% in September 2026. Strategic oil reserves and growing electric-vehicle adoption offer some protection, but weak domestic demand, a prolonged property slump and industrial overcapacity continue to weigh on prices. Factory-gate inflation has surged to 5%, squeezing manufacturers unable to pass on higher costs. Meanwhile, sluggish retail sales are pushing companies to rely on exports. Cheaper Chinese goods could help contain global inflation, but also threaten manufacturers elsewhere, intensifying competition and trade tensions.

Tata Motors has secured 87.8% of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group, crossing the 80% threshold needed to take control after a 15-month acquisition process. The next steps include settling the offer, buying out remaining minority shareholders and beginning integration.

Tata plans to refinance €3.875 billion in acquisition debt over 12-18 months. The deal could generate cost savings through shared engineering, sourcing and distribution networks. It will also give Tata greater global scale, strengthening its presence in Europe and the Americas while preserving Iveco's Turin headquarters and meeting commitments on jobs and manufacturing.

India's share of financially distressed companies has declined, with firms classified as stressed or zombie falling to 14.2% in 2025, according to Dun & Bradstreet. Zombie firms, which struggle to generate enough operating profit to cover interest payments for three consecutive years, remain a concern. About 43% of 971 companies classified as zombies between 2015 and 2025 showed full or temporary recovery, while 25% remained zombies. Construction and textiles had the most such firms, while cement, telecom and media saw higher concentrations. Their persistence can crowd out healthier businesses and weaken economic growth.

That's all from us this week. Subscribe to our newsletters and the website for what's in the news and beyond it. Write to us at newsletters@livemint.com.

data.title: Cathie Wood Loads Up On TEM, ILMN And Biotech Stocks — But Pares Stake In This Pharma Giant That Had A Blowout Q3
data.description:
Key points:
  • ARK's actively managed ETFs made a mix of moves, trimming some established holdings while adding to smaller healthcare names.
  • ARK Genomic Revolution ETF increased its exposure to Tempus AI, Pacific Biosciences of California, Beam Therapeutics, and Arcturus Therapeutics.
  • Eli Lilly was among ARK’s notable trims on Friday, with its flagship ARK Innovation ETF paring its position despite Lilly’s blowout third-quarter performance.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest made a series of moves across its actively managed ETFs on Friday, with the firm adding to several healthcare, genomics and cryptocurrency stocks.

ARK's actively managed ETFs made a mix of moves, trimming some established holdings while adding to smaller healthcare names. Several stocks appeared in more than one fund.

ARK Loads Up On Biotech Stocks

Tempus AI Inc. (TEM) was one of ARK’s more prominent biotech-related purchases. ARK added 61,114 shares through ARK Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG) and another 93,407 shares through ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), increasing its exposure to the AI-powered healthcare and genomics company across two funds.

Illumina Inc. (ILMN) was another significant addition, with ARKK buying 43,130 shares of the genomics sequencing company.

ARKG also added to several other biotechnology names, buying 133,767 shares of Pacific Biosciences of California Inc. (PACB), 22,687 shares of Beam Therapeutics Inc. (BEAM) and 64,483 shares of Arcturus Therapeutics Holdings Inc. (ARCT). ARKK separately bought another 346,507 shares of Pacific Biosciences.

Outside healthcare and genomics, ARK added to Circle Internet Group Inc. (CRCL) and Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN) across multiple ETFs. ARK Blockchain & Fintech Innovation ETF (ARKF) also bought 13,757 shares of Robinhood Markets Inc. (HOOD).

ARK’s Surprise Sell

Eli Lilly & Co. (LLY) was among the notable positions ARK pared on Friday. ARK’s flagship ARKK ETF sold 17,626 shares of the pharmaceutical giant.

The move came after Lilly reported third-quarter results that topped expectations, with the company continuing to benefit from strong demand for its diabetes and obesity medicines.

ARK also reduced its exposure to CareDx Inc. (CDNA), with the ARKG ETF selling 50,859 shares.

Bullish (BLSH) was another recurring sell. ARK sold shares of the crypto-focused financial services company through ARKF, ARKK and ARKW, with the trades totaling more than 238,000 shares across the three ETFs.

ARKG’s price fell nearly 7% in Friday’s regular trading session. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around ARKG trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Weather today: New depression to bring heavy rain to Andhra, Kerala; no showers for Delhi - Check full IMD forecast
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast rain, thunderstorms, and gusty winds across several states on Saturday, October 31, amid a warning that a new weather system is brewing in the Bay of Bengal, even as the remnants of Cyclone Arnab continue to impact inland areas.

Areas including Arunachal Pradesh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala may experience heavy rainfall, while thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds are expected in states such as Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karnataka, and Telangana.

Delhi, meanwhile, is expected to see partly cloudy skies, with no rainfall.

No rainfall is expected in Delhi today, October 31, a day after the city recorded its lowest October day temperature in 75 years, with the maximum plunging to 20.7 degrees Celsius amid two days of persistent rain.

Delhi is, however, expected to experience a partly cloudy sky with winds blowing from the northwest and southeast at 5-10 kmph.

"The maximum and minimum temperatures over Delhi are likely to be in the range of 26 degC to 28 degC and 15 degC to 17 degC respectively," IMD noted

On Friday, Delhi also recorded its wettest October day in four years and the sixth-wettest since 1951. The city also logged its cleanest October air on Friday, with the AQI settling at 60, the lowest since October 10, 2022, when it was 44.

The IMD warned of a new weather system brewing in the Bay of Bengal. A low-pressure area lying over the South Andaman Sea and adjoining regions is intensifying today.

"It is very likely to concentrate into a Depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands and the Andaman Sea around 31 October," the Met Dept said in its official release.

Following this development, the system is expected to move westward and then northward toward the Andhra Pradesh coast over the next two days.

Meanwhile, yesterday's well-marked low-pressure area-the remnant of Cyclone Arnab-has weakened and currently lies over north Chhattisgarh and adjoining East Madhya Pradesh.

Heavy Rain Alerts: Isolated heavy rainfall is expected in Arunachal Pradesh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala.

Severe Thunderstorms (40-50 kmph winds): Lightning and strong gusty winds are likely to hit Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal.

Moderate Thunderstorms (30-40 kmph winds): Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Interior Karnataka are expected to experience lightning and gusty winds, with strong surface winds, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

General Thunderstorms: Isolated lightning and thunderstorms are expected across Coastal Karnataka and Chhattisgarh.

West Bengal shifted 12,000 people living along the Sankosh in Alipurduar district to safety, while Assam closely monitored the situation in vulnerable areas of Dhubri and Kokrajhar districts after the river's water level rose following a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in adjoining Bhutan, officials said.

Water level in the Sankosh, which forms the inter-state boundary between Assam and West Bengal, rose by nearly two feet since this morning after a glacial lake in Bhutan's Gasa region burst its banks on Thursday evening.

The incident triggered flood alerts in parts of north Bengal and Assam, with authorities keeping a close watch on the water levels of rivers flowing down from the Himalayan kingdom.

data.title: GAIL gets board nod to list GAIL Gas, proposes up to 25% stake dilution
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- State-owned GAIL (India) Ltd has given in-principle approval to list its wholly owned subsidiary GAIL Gas Ltd on Indian stock exchanges through an initial public offering (IPO), with a proposal to dilute up to 25 per cent of its equity in the company.

In an exchange filing on Friday, GAIL said its board had approved the listing of GAIL Gas shares through the IPO route. The proposal marks a step towards bringing the subsidiary to the public markets, although the final structure and extent of the stake sale are yet to be decided.

The filing said the IPO would involve "diluting GAIL's equity in GGL upto 25%". It added that GAIL Gas would submit a final proposal based on recommendations from the Book Running Lead Managers (BRLMs), covering valuation, price band, the mode of the offering and other terms and conditions.

The final extent of dilution, along with the IPO structure and other terms, will require approval from the GAIL board. The company said the details would be communicated to the stock exchanges after they are finalised.

The development comes as GAIL reported revenue from operations of Rs 45,924 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 38,981 crore in the first quarter. Profit before tax (PBT) stood at Rs 5,838 crore, against Rs 5,773 crore in the preceding quarter, while profit after tax (PAT) increased to Rs 4,650 crore from Rs 4,292 crore.

For the first half of FY27, the company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 84,905 crore from Rs 69,824 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

The company's PBT for April-September 2026 stood at Rs 11,611 crore, against Rs 5,357 crore in the year-ago period. PAT during the first half increased to Rs 8,943 crore from Rs 4,104 crore in the corresponding period of FY26.

data.title: Quess Corp Q2 net profit jumps 44% to ₹74.66 crore
data.description:
Staffing and workforce solutions provider Quess Corp on Friday reported a 44.21 per cent year-on-year growth in consolidated net profit to ₹74.66 crore during the September quarter of the current fiscal.

The company's net profit stood at ₹51.77 crore during the corresponding period of the preceding financial year, Quess Corp said in a regulatory filing.

Revenue from operations grew by 14.74 per cent during the quarter under review to ₹4,396.48 crore, compared to ₹3,831.60 crore in the same period a year ago.

The company’s board of directors also approved an interim dividend of ₹5 per share, Quess Corp informed the stock exchanges.

"The Board has approved an interim dividend of ₹5 per share, reaffirming our commitment to creating sustainable value for our shareholders. This quarter's performance was marked by a significant milestone as our headcount crossed 5,00,000, driven largely by headcount additions of over 20,000 in our General Staffing business," Quess Corp ED and Group CEO Lohit Bhatia said.

He said the segment delivered robust performance, adding 116 new client logos and achieving 15 per cent YoY revenue growth and 23 per cent YoY Ebitda growth, positioning us strongly for the quarters ahead.

“Professional Staffing recorded 13 per cent revenue growth, supported by sustained hiring demand from Global Capability Centres (GCCs).

“Despite geopolitical challenges in the Middle East, our Overseas Business maintained momentum, delivering 10 per cent YoY revenue growth and 23per cent YoY Ebitda growth. This performance was driven by higher margins in the Middle East, while Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines contributed to revenue growth," Bhatia added.

data.title: Open digital infra has critical role to play in accelerating digitalisation of retail sector: DPIIT Secretary
data.description:
Open digital infrastructure has a critical role to play in accelerating the digitalisation of India's retail ecosystem, particularly its vast network of kirana stores, a top government official said on Friday.

Addressing a programme on digitisation of trade, Secretary in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) Amardeep Singh Bhatia said that ONDC's DigiDukaan is an important step in this direction.

By bringing together retailers, FMCG companies and distributors on a common network, DPIIT, along with ONDC, is helping build a more connected and efficient general trade ecosystem, creating a pathway for digitalisation to reach kiranas at scale, he said.

"Open digital infrastructure has a critical role to play in accelerating the digitalisation of India's retail ecosystem, particularly its vast network of kirana stores," Bhatia said.

ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce) DigiDukaan addresses procurement by digitising kiranas as buyers.

Through a single digital interface, retailers can discover and order products across multiple brands, distributors and wholesalers, with greater visibility into pricing, trade schemes and product availability.

Senior representatives from Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Coca-Cola India, ITC, P&G, Marico, CavinKare, Pidilite, Britannia, Adani Wilmar, LT Foods, Anmol Industries, Haldiram's, Emami, Veeba and Nilon's participated in the roundtable, along with representatives from logistics providers and technology partners.

DigiDukaan has connected over 21,000 retailers with more than 450 brands across Hyderabad, Jaipur and Mumbai as of September.

Speaking at the roundtable, Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said, "ONDC's DigiDukaan shows that when open digital infrastructure is built around the needs of the small retailer, adoption follows."

data.title: JioStar Q2 PAT falls 13.2% to ₹1,147 crore; revenue rises 9.8%
data.description:
Media and entertainment platform JioStar reported a 13.2 per cent decline in profit after tax (PAT) to ₹1,147 crore in the September quarter of FY27, even as gross revenue rose 9.8 per cent to ₹7,944 crore.

JioStar reported a PAT of ₹1,322 crore and gross revenue of ₹7,232 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.

Revenue from operations rose 10.1 per cent year-on-year to ₹6,806 crore, according to the earnings statement of Reliance Industries Ltd.

The revenue growth was "led by strong growth in subscription revenue and Digital Entertainment Ad revenue", the company said.

JioStar is a joint venture formed following the merger of the media businesses of Reliance Industries and the India business of global media and entertainment company Walt Disney.

Its streaming platform JioHotstar Monthly Active Users (MAUs) averaged "440 million during the quarter, a growth of 10 per cent Y-o-Y," it added.

During the quarter, it relaunched and rebranded ‘JioHotstar’ in international markets of Singapore, the UK and Canada. "Active subscriber volume in these markets has grown by 30 per cent since the launch," it added.

In the September quarter, entertainment watch-time on JioHotstar grew more than 15 per cent, driven by strong performance across Hindi and regional markets, the statement said.

JioStar said its sports portfolio remained a key highlight during the September quarter, led by marquee international cricket series between England and India, Wimbledon, the US Open and the ongoing Premier League season.

The England-India series delivered strong digital viewership, emerging as the biggest-ever bilateral overseas series on JioHotstar, the company said.

data.title: EVs, CNG and CBG: Why India’s clean mobility transition also needs an agricultural lens
data.description:
India’s clean-mobility debate is usually staged as a contest between machines: batteries against cylinders, electric against CNG. It is the wrong contest. The better question is what vehicle runs on, and where that energy comes from and the answer could lead to the paddy fields of Punjab and Haryana.

Numbers are encouraging but incomplete. Electric vehicles make up about 11 per cent of all vehicle sales in 2026, and nearly 43 per cent of passenger three-wheelers sold in the first seven months of this year were electric. For short, stop-start city trips, the battery is winning. But electric buses were under 5 per cent of sales and heavy trucks just 0.4 per cent.

An electric vehicle is also only as clean as the power that charges it. Coal and lignite supplied about two-thirds of India’s electricity in the July to September quarter of FY 2026, and officials expect coal to provide about half of generation as late as 2035-36.

The life-cycle reality

This is why a recent TERI study on vehicular emission becomes important. It compared petrol, diesel, CNG, electricity and LNG across six vehicle categories over their full life cycles. Electric mobility offered favourable economics for two- and three-wheelers and certain urban uses, while CNG gave a competitive mix of affordability, life-cycle performance and practicality for cars, taxis, buses and several light commercial applications. The life-cycle record of EVs remains sensitive to electricity generation and battery manufacturing. The lesson is not one fuel, but the right fuel for each vehicle.

That is where compressed biogas (CBG) fits in. It is produced by digesting crop residue, dung and organic waste in sealed tanks, making CBG interchangeable with CNG, which can run through the same pipelines and engines. TERI’s earlier assessment found it can be carbon-negative: up to 1.141 kg of CO₂ equivalent avoided per kilometre for a four-wheeler, the result of avoided methane leakage from unmanaged dung and of digestate replacing synthetic fertiliser. The study estimates that blending 20 % CBG into CNG could make the fuel carbon-neutral over its life cycle. Same fact was also highlighted by Niti Aayog in its Net Zero Report for the Transport Sector released in February 2026.

In fact, an earlier NRI report states that a single CBG plant can eliminate 11,000-12,000 kilograms of PM emissions annually, which is equivalent to emission savings from 1.5-1.75 lac EVs or that achieved by removing 25000 older vehicles from the roads.

The agricultural lens matters because of the feedstock issue. Punjab and Haryana together produce about 29 million tonnes of paddy straw, which are sometimes burnt because the window for sowing wheat after the paddy harvest is extremely short. While the official picture on emissions from stubble has improved, tens of millions of tonnes of residue need a permanent, paying destination, that fines and machines cannot supply.

A prize not a penalty

A CBG plant offers farmers a price for straw instead of a penalty for burning it, villages get a local employer and soil a nutrient-rich digestate. While policy has helped in building demand—blending obligations is set at 1 per cent in 2025-26, 3 per cent in 2026-27, 4 per cent in 2027-28 and 5 per cent from 2028-29 yet existing plants are reported to run at only 20 to 60 per cent of capacity, The reason: feedstock is seasonal and collection is fragmented and year-round aggregation of biomass, long-term offtake contracts and simpler clearances would change that.

None of this competes with the electric future. Electrons for two- and three-wheelers and urban fleets, increasingly green gas for heavier, high-mileage vehicles, and the farm as supplier of one and beneficiary of the other. The test is not which technology wins but whether every vehicle runs on the cleanest energy available to it.

India’s mobility transition will not only be decided in showrooms and power stations, but in the fields, by what we do with the straw left behind after harvest.

data.title: Fitch Affirms Slovakia at ’A-’ with Stable Outlook
data.description:
Fitch Ratings affirmed Slovakia’s long-term foreign-currency Issuer Default Rating at A- with a Stable Outlook on October 30, 2026, citing the country’s deep integration with the euro area and continued EU fund inflows despite mounting budget pressures.

However, fiscal consolidation is expected to lose momentum ahead of the 2027 parliamentary election, with the deficit projected to widen to 5.0% of GDP in 2027 before improving from 2028.

The deterioration reflects higher public-sector wages, social spending, defense expenditure, and debt-servicing costs.

Still, an average debt maturity of over eight years helps contain near-term refinancing risks.

GDP growth is projected to grow by 0.8% in 2026 amid higher energy prices and financing costs linked to Middle East tensions.

Growth is forecast to strengthen gradually to 1.8% by 2028, on rising automotive production and stronger investment.

Other major agencies keep stable outlooks, with S&P rating Slovakia A, Moody’s A3, and DBRS A (low).

data.title: Bank holiday today 31 Oct 2026: Are banks open today? Check if SBI, HDFC, ICICI Bank and others are open in your city
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Bank branches across most parts of India will remain open today, Saturday, 31 October 2026. However, customers in Gujarat will have to account for a regional bank holiday marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Although 31 October falls on a Saturday, it is the fifth Saturday of the month. Under the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) banking holiday rules, all scheduled and non-scheduled banks remain closed on the second and fourth Saturdays, while other Saturdays are regular working days unless a separate state-specific holiday has been declared.

Here's what you need to know about bank closures in your city today, 31 October 2026.

Banks in Gujarat will remain closed on 31 October on account of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday. The holiday is included in the Gujarat government's official bank holiday calendar for 2026.

The Government of Gujarat notified the list of public holidays for banks in the state for 2026 under Notification No. GS/22/2025/JSR/2025/509/GH, dated 27 November 2025.

The notification states: "The Government of Gujarat, in consultation with Reserve Bank of India, Ahmedabad, is pleased to declare the following days to be public holidays for banks in Gujarat during the year 2026."

It specifically lists Saturday, 31 October 2026, as a public holiday for banks on account of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday.

This means bank branches in Ahmedabad and all parts of Gujarat will remain closed today. The holiday applies to both public-sector and private-sector bank branches in the state, including SBI, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank.

According to the RBI holiday calendar, banks will operate normally in Bengaluru, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Chennai, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, New Delhi, Patna, Thiruvananthapuram, etc.

These cities or states do not have a separate bank holiday notified for 31 October 2026. Since the date is the fifth Saturday, the regular second- and fourth-Saturday closure rule does not apply.

Yes. State-specific bank holidays apply only to banks operating in the notified region.

Therefore, SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank, Axis Bank, and other lenders will keep their branches open today, except in Gujarat.

data.title: Ramalinga Raju who went for a ride on a tiger and stopped smiling thereafter
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- In 2008, Ramalinga Raju had the world at his feet. India's IT industry was poised for take-off, following the boost from the turn-of-the-century Y2K scare, which sent global corporations scrambling to Indian vendors for fixes to their software programmes. The threat proved largely a red herring, but the discovery of Indian IT talent was real. India's software exports had soared from $6.3 billion in 2000-01 to $47 billion in 2008-09, and despite the financial crisis, the long-term outlook was bright.

Satyam Computer Services, the company Raju had founded in 1987, was among the front-runners of this boom. It had closed the previous year with reported revenues of Rs.8,473 crore and profits of Rs.1,688 crore, ranking fourth among India's IT services companies. Its 1992 IPO had rewarded shareholders handsomely, with the stock touching a peak of Rs.544 in May 2008.

Then January 2009 dawned, and another familiar story of entrepreneurial ambition collapsing under the weight of corporate deception burst into the open.

Byrraju Ramalinga Raju, from Bhimavaram in coastal Andhra Pradesh, was an unlikely IT czar. Born into an agricultural family, he graduated in commerce before earning an MBA from Ohio University. On returning to India in 1977, he tried his hand at textiles and construction before starting Satyam with his brother-in-law DVS Raju and just 20 employees. The company surged, eventually employing more than 50,000 people and serving blue-chip clients including General Electric, Nestle and Cisco.

Raju was soon the toast of the industry, serving on prominent industry bodies and chairing Nasscom in 2006-07. Meanwhile, his family ventured into real estate and infrastructure, businesses that would become crucial to his downfall.

On 7 January 2009, Raju stunned investors with a confessional letter admitting that Satyam's books had been systematically cooked. They contained thousands of crores in fictitious cash and bank balances, accrued interest and inflated debtors, alongside large hidden liabilities. The reported operating profit for the September 2008 quarter was Rs.649 crore, while the actual figure was just Rs.61 crore. The gap, he admitted, had grown beyond his ability to manage.

In his letter, he captured the trap he had created for himself: "It was like riding a tiger, not knowing how to get off without being eaten."

The immediate trigger was a proposal for Satyam to buy 100% of the family firm Maytas Properties for $1.3 billion and take a 51% stake in Maytas Infrastructure for $300 million. The deal made little strategic sense for Satyam and appeared to offer a way of converting the company's purported cash reserves into tangible assets owned by the promoter family. Raju later acknowledged that the acquisition was a last-ditch attempt to cover fictitious assets with real ones.

The board approved the proposal, but investors reacted furiously to what they saw as a blatant conflict of interest. The deal was withdrawn the next day. Satyam's American depositary receipts plunged, while the backlash was compounded by the World Bank's decision to bar the company from certain business for improper benefits and the departure of independent directors.

The global financial crisis and a deteriorating outlook for IT spending added to the pressure. The final push came when investment bank DSP Merrill Lynch, engaged to explore ways of enhancing shareholder value, flagged financial discrepancies and alerted the market regulator.

The Maytas fiasco did not create the fraud; it exposed the desperation behind it. The Central Bureau of Investigation later uncovered thousands of fabricated invoices, while scrutiny revealed that even Satyam's reported headcount and operating performance had been exaggerated. The company's stock collapsed, wiping out Rs.13,655 crore of shareholder wealth.

Raju resigned on 7 January and was arrested two days later, along with his brother and Satyam managing director, B. Rama Raju. The government dissolved the board and appointed new directors to stabilise the company.

In April 2015, a special CBI court convicted Ramalinga Raju and nine others in the fraud case, sentencing them to seven years' imprisonment. Separately, Sebi imposed a 14-year market ban. The audit partners also faced disciplinary action, even as the independence and oversight of auditors came under scrutiny. Raju was granted bail after his conviction, with his sentence suspended pending appeal. He has since largely withdrawn from public life.

Satyam itself disappeared into the folds of Tech Mahindra, which bought the stricken company following a government-supervised bidding process in 2009. But the Satyam name has become synonymous with corporate fraud.

Had Ramalinga Raju stayed the course with India's IT story, he could have made billions. Instead, he chose to ride a tiger.

For more such stories, read The Enterprising Indian: Stories From India Inc.

data.title: Here's why Granules India shares could see a reaction on Monday
data.description:
Granules India shares will be in focus on Monday (November 2) after the company reported that the US FDA has issued Form 483 to the company's Hyderabad Unit with 11 observations after concluding a GMP inspection at a Hyderabad facility. This confirms the CNBC-TV18 newsbreak. Earlier on October 19, CNBC-TV18 had reported that the US FDA began an audit of Gagillapur. CNBC-TV18 had reached out to Granules for a comment.

CNBC-TV18 Newsbreak Confirmed

In an exchange filing issued on Saturday, October 31, the company said that the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) concluded a current Good Manufacturing Practice inspection of its finished dosage facility at Gagillapur, Hyderabad. The inspection, as mentioned before, concluded with the issuance of Form 483 with a total of 11 observations.

The said inspection was conducted from October 19 to October 30, 2026.

As per the US drug regulator, an FDA Form 483 is issued to a company when an FDA investigator has observed any violations of the Food, Drug and Cosmetic (FD&C) Act and related Acts.

Observations are conducted when, in the investigator's assessment, the conditions or practices noted suggest that any food, drug, device, or cosmetic has been adulterated or is being prepared, packaged, or stored in a manner that could lead to adulteration or pose a health risk.

Company's Reaction

The Telangana-based company said that this was the first USFDA inspection of the facility since the Warning Letter of February 26, 2025, which followed an inspection in August-September 2024.

For its part, the company has claimed that none of the observations was related to data integrity or cross-contamination.

Furthermore, according to Granules, the observations concern the enhancements in investigations, change control, process and equipment qualification, visual-inspection controls and documentation practices.

The company further added that there is no impact on manufacturing or distribution of products from the site. In addition, Granules also added that the company will submit a 'comprehensive' response to the US drug agency within 15 days.

Commenting on the inspection, Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati, Chairman and Managing Director, said: “The inspection progressed constructively, and the observations are of a nature that we believe can be fully addressed through our responses and corrective and preventive actions. Quality is the foundation of everything we do at Granules, and we will continue to engage transparently with the agency.”

Ahead Of Q2 Results

The company will be reporting its results for the second quarter or Q2FY27 on November 2. Ahead of that, when we look at its performance in Q1, the pharma company's Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) for the June quarter rose by 37.4% YoY to ₹339 crore from ₹246.5 crore.

The EBITDA margin expanded by over 300 basis points to 23% from 20.3% YoY. Granules India's net profit for the period increased by 60% year-on-year to ₹180 crore from ₹112.60 crore. Revenue grew 22% to ₹1,476 crore from ₹1,210 crore during Q1 of FY26.

Stock Performance

When we look at the performance of the pharma company's stock, the shares of the company closed in the green on Friday, with minimal gains of 0.29%. In this year's trade so far, the stock price has expanded its value by over 35%.

Furthermore, the stock is at over 9% below its 52-week high of ₹923.65 and sitting with a cushion of 58.49% above its 52-week low of ₹529.85. The stock has made major gains over the past week and has closed in the green in 7 out of the last 10 trading sessions.

data.title: Can India afford tax cuts right now?
data.description:
With just about three months to the budget, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is likely to be swamped with demands for more funds or tax relief. One of the loudest is the clamour for a cut in long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) and securities transaction tax (STT). Stock investors argue that a tax cut will bring back foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) who have yanked out a staggering $32.5 billion from Indian equities this year.

The big question for Sitharaman is whether the exchequer can afford tax cuts amidst rising expenses and ballooning debt.

There's an estimated ₹2.85 lakh crore fiscal hole as subsidy bills surge and tax collections slide, according to ICRA, a Mumbai-based ratings agency. That's more than double the revenue from LTCG in the financial year ended March 2025.

How bad could India's balance of payments get? 

Meanwhile, the dollar exodus from the share market has worsened the country's balance of payments (BoP), the difference between money coming into the country and the sum that leaves. A net outflow of money of $50 billion to $55 billion in the second half of the year could keep the rupee under pressure, says Madhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay Global, a Mumbai broking firm.

The Reserve Bank of India has already spent $67 billion over the last 8 weeks to keep the rupee afloat. That's nearly half of the $144 billion ammunition parked with Indian banks, and subsidised by the regulator, which would be due for repayment in less than three years.

"Excluding FCNR(B), you would be looking at, you know, multiple years of a BOP deficit, which becomes a source of, let's say, financial stability risks and all of that," Dhiraj Nim said.

"Unlike the last time this happened around 2013, this is not so much a homegrown problem. This is happening because of certain global factors which have weighed on flows into India."DHIRAJ NIM, ECONOMIST, ANZ

If the FPI selling continues, and the government remains intent on not letting the currency slide to ₹100/dollar, the RBI will have to spend even more of its forex reserves.

LTCG hike didn't start the FPI sell-off, a cut may not stop it

Indeed, the sell-off in Indian stocks started in the fall of 2024 because Indian stocks had run up too much, too fast, and global investors found them expensive. There were juicy profits to be taken out of India, and the AI trade in other countries offered the investors a relatively lucrative opportunity to put their capital to work. Then came the US-Iran war, which drove up oil prices past the $100 mark, squeezing vulnerable economies like India.

Stock valuations have corrected enough already, and an LTCG cut in India will not stop the US-Iran war, nor will it birth large language models or memory chip makers overnight.

Pain relief for a few, austerity for many 

It may offer some pain relief to bleeding portfolios, but the government has other responsibilities too. "The government is cutting expenses elsewhere. For example, some of the water scheme, some of the housing scheme, and so on and so forth," HSBC's Pranjul Bhandari said. These cuts affect the poorer sections of society, most of whom may not have a stake in the stock market.

Cutting spending on essentials when inflation is rising may be politically costly. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's rivals would have more material to escalate their attacks on the administration.

The country has less than 63 million unique people with investments in mutual funds, according to the August data released by the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI). A much larger base of voters with no investable surplus is reeling from the high cost of food, fuel, and fertilisers.

The government has already seen its tax revenue dip 23% in the first five months of this fiscal year due to duty cuts in petrol and diesel. ICRA expects the fiscal deficit (the difference between the government's expenses and revenue) to be at least ₹1.3 lakh more than what it had budgeted for in February this year. That's as much as the LTCG collected in FY25.

The end of the war in West Asia would be enough to spur a sharp correction in oil prices, which would in turn reduce inflation, cap the cost of capital, and improve earnings growth for Indian companies, making them attractive again for FPIs. That's a tide the Indian government can't turn.

data.title: Ex-SC Judge to Mediate Dispute Between Govt & RIL Consortium Over K-G Gas
data.description:
Indu Bhan New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday appointed former judge Ranjana Prakash Desai as the sole mediator to resolve the long-running $1.73 billion Krishna-Godavari basin gas migration dispute between a Reliance Industries-led consortium and the government, after the two sides failed to reach an amicable settlement in the case.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi referred the matter for mediation after attorney general R Venkataramani informed that the parties were unable to arrive at a "viable solution". The bench said Justice Desai, a former judge of the top court, could take assistance from two domain experts as may be suggested by the parties to facilitate the mediation process.

The two sides assured the court that they would extend full cooperation to the mediator. The court will take up the case again after four weeks and check the progress of the mediation. The SC was hearing three appeals filed by Reliance Industries and its partners- BP Exploration (Alpha) of the UK and Canada-based Niko (NECO) - against a February 2025 decision of the Delhi High Court, which set aside a 2018 international arbitration ruling favouring the consortium in the dispute. The high court held that the arbitration award was contrary to the settled position of law.

data.title: Inflation, Poor Monsoon Hurt Liquor Spends: USL
data.description:
Aanya Thakur Mumbai: Inflation and a weaker monsoon are weighing on lower-income urban consumers, posing a challenge for United Spirits as the Diageo-controlled liquor maker seeks to revive growth in its mass-market portfolio while banking on premiumisation to drive sales. "India 1, the bottom end, the India 1 consumer, which is a target audience for the lower half of the IMFL portfolio, is showing signs of fatigue due to the impact of inflation on their wallets," chief executive Praveen Someshwar said during the company's September-quarter earnings call. "India 2 and India 3 are robust and holding up." The strain is also visible in the company's lower-priced portfolio, where regulatory changes are adding additional pressures.

United Spirits' popular segment reported a 22.7% decline in net sales value to 181 crore in the quarter, accounting for about 6% of revenue. The business was hit by adverse policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka.

The company's prestige and above portfolio grew 6%, making up 94% of revenue. The Smirnoff maker said it has no immediate plans to intervene in its popular portfolio, largely comprising McDowell's rum, even as CFO Pradeep Jain acknowledged that future profit and growth pools lay in higher-priced brands. "The category will probably die a natural death, so as of now we don't want to make any interventions," he added.

Cost inflation is another pressure point. The West Asia conflict has added about 50 crore to costs in the quarter, affecting glass, energy, packaging and logistics. Extra neutral alcohol prices have also started rising on account of El NiÃ±o's impact on monsoons and crop inflation, the company said.

It expects lower Scotch import duties under the India-UK free trade agreement to offset the ENA cost in the coming quarter. "Hopefully, this will be neutralised by the full effect of the FTA benefit," said Jain, adding that impact beyond the next quarter was "very difficult to call out." The FTA benefit comes amid a directorate of revenue intelligence investigation into the classification of Scotch imports.

data.title: JioStar Net Declines 13% to 1,147 crore in Sept Quarter

Saloni Shukla reports. 8 growth weak at 12.2% after excluding foreign currency windfall Saloni Shukla Mumbai: The sharp rebound in bank deposit growth during the September quarter appears to mask continued difficulties in domestic deposit mobilisation, as the growth was temporarily inflated by the Reserve Bank of India's special Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) swap window.

An analysis of 10 banks shows that reported deposit growth averaged 21.1% year-on-year during July-September. However, excluding the special foreign currency inflows, domestic deposit growth was estimated at just 12.2%-a massive gap of nearly nine percentage points. A similar trend was seen in lending. Reported credit growth averaged 24.2%, but excluding loans linked to the central bank's special window, it was an estimated 18.9%, a difference of more than five percentage points.

The divergence suggests that underlying deposit mobilisation remains weaker than headline numbers indicate, particularly as growth in low-cost current and savings account deposits continues to lag overall deposit growth. At the banking-system level, RBI data showed that deposit growth of 17.8% at September-end continued to trail credit growth of 19.4%, despite extraordinary foreign-currency inflows. Deposit growth subsequently moderated to 16.7% by October 15, while credit growth remained higher at 18.2%. Credit-deposit ratio stood at 81.6%. Among individual lenders, RBL Bank reported deposit growth of 34% during the quarter, which moderated to just 6% when FCNR (B) deposits were excluded.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's deposit growth fell to 13% from 23.2%, while ICICI Bank's declined to 17% from 27.1%. HDFC Bank reported 18.8% deposit growth, including a four-percentage-point contribution from the special window.

The impact was also visible on the lending side. ICICI Bank's reported advances growth of 30% moderated to 24.1% after excluding FCNR(B)-backed lending, while Axis Bank's growth of about 23% fell to nearly 19% on its adjusted measure. The special window, which closed on August 31, helped banks collectively mobilise nearly $133 billion in FCNR (B) deposits.

Banks are now looking to deploy the surplus liquidity into fresh lending over the next two quarters while simultaneously reducing their reliance on expensive wholesale deposits and borrowings. "We are carrying some amount of excess liquidity currently, and I would expect that to be kind of deployed over the next two quarters," Anindya Banerjee, chief financial officer at ICICI Bank, said during the lender's September-quarter earnings call. Kotak Mahindra Bank similarly expects its FCNR (B)liquidity to support incremental lending over the coming quarters, in addition to growth funded by regular deposits. "The FCNR (B) deployment will be in addition to the core deployment from the core deposit," said Devang Gheewalla, group chief financial officer at Kotak Mahindra Bank. He indicated that the bank would deploy the remaining liquidity into customer assets over the next few quarters.

RBL Bank is also looking to expand its wholesale and secured retail businesses using the additional liquidity. The bank has already used part of the funds to retire expensive borrowings and bulk deposits, while temporarily deploying the balance into short-term investments and corporate loans.The inflows have temporarily eased competition for domestic deposits.

According to the RBI's October Bulletin, weighted average rates on fresh domestic term deposits moderated by 40 basis points during April-August, driven partly by foreign-currency inflows and surplus liquidity. A basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point. However, the underlying challenge of building granular deposit franchises remains. With the special FCNR (B) deposit window now closed, the challenge for lenders will be to sustain domestic deposit mobilisation while funding continued demand for corporate, working-capital and retail loans. RBI data showed that deposit growth of 17.8% at Sept-end continued to trail credit growth of 19.4%

data.title: JK Lakshmi Cement Launches Assam Project
data.description:
Bikash Singh Guwahati: JK Lakshmi Cement, held the groundbreaking of Project 'Kamakshi', its first footprint in Assam, at Umrangso village in Dima Hasao district on Friday. Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma attended the event.

Project Kamakshi will be an integrated cement plant with railway sidings. The plant will have a cement capacity of 2.5 million tonnes per annum, supported by a 1 million tonne clinkerisation unit, and is being developed with a total investment of 11,000 crore, including the mining lease. The project is targeted for completion by FY 2029. and will have a future workforce of over 2,000 people, catering primarily to the North East market.

Vinita Singhania, chairperson and managing director, JK Lakshmi Cement, said, "Project Kamakshi is the start of a long-term relationship with Assam and the wider Northeast. This is a region that is building fast, and it deserves quality cement made close to home. With this plant, we want to bring scale, jobs, and dependable supply to the region.

data.title: Delhivery Swings to Black as Revenue Rises 20% in 2nd Qtr
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: New-age logistics company Delhivery reported a 20% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue at 3,066 crore for the September quarter, led by growth in its transport services business. This comprises its ecommerce shipment and part-truck load transportation verticals.

The Gurugram-based company posted a net profit of 41 crore during the three month period, compared to a 50 crore net loss in the same quarter last year. The turnaround in Delhivery's bottomline was consistent with its improving unit economics over the last few quarters.

In the April-June period, it reported 32 crore in net profit. Express parcel, or the ecommerce shipment business, reported a 32% year-on-year volume growth and a 22% revenue growth during the September quarter. This is Delhivery's biggest business vertical. "Express volumes grew 32% YoY in Q2FY27 and 43% YoY in H1FY27, reflecting continued market share gains and the strength of our value proposition across a broad and diversified customer base.

While it remains early to comment on the remainder of Q3FY27, October volumes have exceeded our initial expectations, providing an encouraging start to Q3," the company said in its letter to the shareholders. The October-December quarter of 2026 is expected to be a strong period for logistics and ecommerce companies given that most of the festive shopping period falls during these months.

Delhivery said it will focus on four key initiatives to sustain growth through the rest of FY27 and beyond. These include expanding the geographic reach of its same-day and next-day delivery network, deepening adoption of its integrated warehousing and transportation services among ecommerce clients, and broadening its aggregator and franchise partner programmes.

The company also plans to introduce new products and value-added services on its Delhivery One and Delhivery Direct platforms to onboard more small and medium enterprises (SMEs), micro-SMEs and individual consumers. Delhivery's listed rival Shadowfax on Thursday reported a 57% year-on-year (YoY) increase in operating revenue to 1,538 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with 982 crore in the year-ago period.

Its net profit rose fivefold to 68 crore in Q2 of the 2027 fiscal compared to 13 crore reported a year earlier. During the company's earnings call, Delhivery's CEO Sahil Barua said it will keep investing in growth while continuing to gain market share in the third-party logistics market.

data.title: PB Fintech Q2 Profit Rises 43% to 192cr
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, reported a 43% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to 192.39 crore in the September quarter, driven by strong growth in its core insurance marketplace business and higher renewal income, even as the company continued investing in newer businesses.

Net profit stood at 134.89 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, profit increased 18% from 162.91 crore in the June quarter. Revenue from operations grew 35% to 2,177.71 crore from 1,613.55 crore a year prior. On a sequential basis, revenue increased 15% from 1,888.28 crore. The growth was led by Policybazaar's insurance distribution business, where demand for health and term insurance remained strong.

Total insurance premiums rose 38% to 9,385 crore, with new protection premiums increasing 42%. New health insurance premiums grew 46% YoY. Revenue from its core online businesses, comprising Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, increased 39% to 1,336 crore. Within this, insurance revenue rose 42% to 1,211 crore, while credit revenue grew 19% to 125 crore.

Renewal and trail revenue, which represents recurring income from existing insurance and credit customers, increased 42% to 1,097 crore on a trailing 12-month basis. This has become an important contributor to profitability as the company's customer base expands. Paisabazaar's core loan disbursements rose 22% to 2,791 crore, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth.

Meanwhile, revenue from newer initiatives grew 28% to 842 crore, led by its offline insurance distribution platform PB Partners and international operations. PB Partners' revenue rose 39% to 698 crore, while its active advisor network expanded 55% to 131,000.

However, adjusted Ebitda (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) losses in newer businesses widened to 42 crore from 27 crore, reflecting investments including in PB Pay and Pensionbazaar. At the consolidated level, adjusted Ebitda increased 39% to 216 crore. Total expenses rose 33% to 2,067.66 crore, with advertising and promotional expenditure climbing 59%. data.title: Omron Making in Chennai, Soon for the World
data.description:
Rica Bhattacharyya Mumbai: Omron Healthcare aims to establish Chennai as an international manufacturing hub, said its president and CEO Ayumu Okada, even though the Japanese maker of blood pressure monitors and nebulisers has earmarked the initial output from its newly established Indian facility near the Tamil Nadu capital for domestic sales.

The Kyoto-headquartered company, which has started full-scale production at its first manufacturing facility in India near Chennai, is aiming to reach an annual capacity of 3 million blood pressure monitors by 2028, as it looks to tap the country's largely underpenetrated home blood pressure monitoring market. "India remains an important growth market for us, with significant opportunities to expand home blood pressure monitoring," Okada said. "During the initial phase, 100% of the factory's production output will be allocated to the Indian domestic market." The immediate priority, she said, is to supply products tailored to the needs of Indian consumers in a timely manner, "helping promote wider adoption of home blood pressure monitoring and contributing to efforts to address the country's cardiovascular health challenges". "Over the medium to long term, Omron Healthcare aims to develop Chennai into a manufacturing base supplying healthcare devices to international markets, while strengthening the flexibility and resilience of its global manufacturing network," Okada said.

Despite India's substantial hypertension burden, fewer than 5% of Indian households regularly use a home blood pressure monitor, she said. According to the company's estimates, Omron Healthcare held about 40% of India's home blood pressure monitor market in 2025.

India accounted for around 3% of its global sales in the year ended March 2026. The company's Chennai facility, spanning nearly 24,000 square metres, started full-scale production this month. It has five production lines manufacturing five blood pressure monitor models for the Indian market.

The company has not disclosed the investment in the facility or its expected first-year production volumes. The company is also looking to increase domestic sourcing of components. The Chennai factory carries out assembly through to finished blood pressure monitors in India, drawing on production technologies and quality-control expertise developed at its facilities in Japan and Vietnam. "We are continuing to identify and develop relationships with local suppliers to increase the proportion of components sourced domestically, supporting the government's Make in India initiative," Okada said. Local manufacturing is expected to improve logistical efficiencies and strengthen domestic supply, although the company has not committed to specific retail price reductions.
